name: cloth-reveal
title: Cloth Reveal
description: A satin sheet draped over your content is yanked from one corner, folding and fluttering as a simulated cloth before it clears the frame. The Verlet simulation runs once at load with a fixed timestep and a seeded rest shape (a 32×20 grid), every frame's points are stored, and the timeline only draws the stored frame. The content under the sheet is a neutral lockup with editable text.
useWhen: A logo, product or headline should be unveiled like a launch-event reveal.
The video opens on a covered shape so the viewer waits a beat for what is underneath.
A single premium reveal is the payoff of the video and can afford a heavier render.
avoidWhen: The reveal is a move from one scene to the next rather than content under a sheet: use page-turn.
A light should search the dark stage and land on the logo: use spotlight.
Lines of text only need to rise into place: use mask-reveal-up.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Text
variables.description: Wordmark of the placeholder lockup hidden under the sheet.

variables.label: Direction
variables.description: Which corner is pinched and which way the sheet is pulled.

variables.description: Underside tint, seen where the sheet folds over (hex).

variables.label: Delay
variables.description: Frame (at 30 fps) when the tug starts.

variables.label: Seed
variables.description: Changes the fold pattern and waves of the resting sheet.

variables.label: Speed
variables.description: Scales the timeline after the simulation; it does not change how the cloth moves.
